task_instance: Drive a real browser from the terminal via the bundled playwright-cli wrapper script against a local sample HTML form: open the page, take a snapshot to get element refs, fill in Name/Email fields, click Submit, re-snapshot to confirm the DOM updated, and capture a screenshot artifact.
evidence: Set up scripts/playwright_cli.sh wrapping `npx --yes --package @playwright/cli playwright-cli` per the skill. `npx` and Node/npm were present. Served a local sample.html (form with Name/Email fields and a Submit button that writes a result paragraph via JS) with `python3 -m http.server 8931`. The CLI's default browser (Chrome for Testing / chrome-for-testing channel, bundled chromium rev 1246) was not installed, and `install-browser`/`playwright install` failed because the sandbox's network policy blocks cdn.playwright.dev (403 'request blocked'). Found a pre-installed Chromium (rev 1194, matching the system's global `playwright@1.56.1`) at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome. Worked around the version mismatch (not a safety-rule violation, just local config) by writing .playwright/cli.config.json pointing launchOptions.executablePath at that binary with browserName 'chromium'. Then ran the full documented core workflow: `open http://localhost:8931/sample.html` (succeeded, page title captured), `snapshot` (returned yaml with refs e5 Name textbox, e7 Email textbox, e8 Submit button), `fill e5 'Ada Lovelace'`, `fill e7 'ada@example.com'`, `click e8`, `snapshot` again which showed the DOM updated to 'Submitted: Ada Lovelace / ada@example.com', and `screenshot --filename output/playwright/result.png`. Verified the deliverable: output/playwright/result.png exists and `file` confirms 'PNG image data, 1280 x 720, 8-bit/color RGB, non-interlaced' (15660 bytes). Browser was closed cleanly afterward and the local http server killed. No network egress to external/paid services, no credentials, no MCP/connector tools used, all work confined to the work directory.
